name: Figure Sorting
blurb: Three shapes belong together. Find the fourth.
childIntro: These three shapes are alike in some way. Which one of the answers belongs with them?
howItWorks: Three figures are shown together. They share one hidden rule. The child works out the rule and picks the answer that follows it too. The rule is often not the obvious one: it can be a count, a part inside the shape, or a property like having straight edges.
parentTip: The classic mistake is finding a rule that fits two of the three. Have your child say the rule out loud and then test it against all three shapes before looking at the answers. If a rule only fits two, it is the wrong rule.

questions.prompt: These three go together. Which one belongs with them?

figure.alt: Three shapes: a blue circle, a red circle and a green circle.

questions.explanation: All three are circles. The colours are all different, so colour is not the rule. The rule is round. Only choice a is a circle.
questions.strategy: If one thing changes in all three, that thing is not the rule. Look for what stays the same.
